The Radar Cross Section (RCS) of a target should be decreased by sixteen times to reduce the maximum detection distance by half.
The researchers used the CST software to simulate the application of RAM to different parts of the aircraft.
The FC70 RAM material has good attenuation in the range of 10 to 12 GHz.
The simulations were performed at a frequency of 11.1 GHz, where the material is more sensitive.

The four scenarios evaluated in this study were: Scenario 1: almost covered aircraft, Scenario 2: turbine palettes and exhaust not coated, Scenario 3: air inlet not coated, and Scenario 4: only horizontal and vertical stabilizers coated.
The average RCS reduction in Scenario 1 was around 10 dB of attenuation.
The maximum range of the radar detection before and after applying RAM in Scenario 1 was 222 km and 116 km, respectively.
The average RCS reduction in Scenario 2 was around 7 dB of attenuation.
The maximum range of the radar detection before and after applying RAM in Scenario 2 was 222 km and 169.8 km, respectively.
The critical factor to consider in the design process of a low observable aircraft is the shape of the aircraft.
The typical radar detection distance for an aircraft with a frontal RCS of 5m2 is 165 km of distance.
The theoretical attenuation of the RAM at 11.1 GHz was 22.6 dB.
The researchers used the CATIA software to develop a 3D model of the fighter aircraft.
The simulations were performed using the Asymptotic Solver (A-Solver) package of the CST software.
The Gaussian excitation, vertical polarization, and Triangular Mesh were used in the simulations.
Around 2,000,000 elements were generated in the simulations.
